deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. There are no derivations, formulas or computations. It continues the list headed 'Noch zu lesende Vorlesungen' (lectures still to be given) from the previous page, which is Hilbert's running inventory of courses he planned to teach; items already taught are crossed out. Read from the image, this page has:

(1) '[Ueber die Axiome der Geometrie] und ihre allgemeine erkenntnistheoretische Bedeutung. Für Hörer aller Facultäten.' The opening words 'Ueber die Axiome der Geometrie' are struck through, but the continuation is not. The title was therefore probably reworded rather than marked as taught. The intended course is 'on the axioms of geometry and their general epistemological significance', open to students of all faculties.

(2) 'Theorie der algebraischen Funktionen einer Veränderlichen' (theory of algebraic functions of one variable). It is written smaller, in a lighter hand or pen, so it was probably added later.

(3) 'Partielle Differentialgleichungen der Physik' (partial differential equations of physics). It is in a larger script, also apparently a later addition.

Pencil archival or shelf notes appear at the lower left ('35.4.91', '103 4.n88', reading uncertain). A small number '18' (or '14') is at the lower right.

Context: the list fits Hilbert's Königsberg years (c. 1886–1895). Items on the previous page such as analytic mechanics, elliptic functions and Variationsrechnung are crossed out as completed. The axioms-of-geometry entry fits his developing interest in foundations; he lectured on projective geometry in 1891 and on the foundations of geometry in 1894. The algebraic-functions and PDE-of-physics entries match courses he later gave, the latter mainly at Göttingen.

deep.surprise_reason: This is only an administrative list of planned lecture topics, with no mathematical content. The one mildly interesting detail is the explicitly epistemological framing of an axioms-of-geometry course aimed at all faculties. That is consistent with Hilbert's known early interest in foundations, which is already well documented in the edited Königsberg lecture notes.
transcription_corrections: Only 'Ueber die Axiome der Geometrie' is struck through; 'und ihre allgemeine erkenntnistheoretische Bedeutung' is not, so the entry was reworded rather than wholly cancelled.
'Erkenntnisstheoretische' is Hilbert's spelling (Erkenntnis(s)theoretische), with the line break 'all-gemeine'.
'Theorie der algebraischen Funktionen einer Veränderlichen' is written in a smaller, lighter hand and is likely a later addition.
The last line reads 'Partielle Differentialgleichungen der Physik' (the 's' is written as a long s, making it look like 'Phyrik').
The pencil notes at the bottom left ('35.4.91', '103 4.n88') are probably later archival or foliation marks, not Hilbert's text; the reading is uncertain.
The small number at the bottom right may be '14' rather than '18'.
